route.text: Use MIT's own first-year application portal. University enrollment normally requires the transfer route; limited alternate-calendar exceptions may apply. International applicants usually apply during their final secondary-school year. MIT evaluates the original grading system.

rounds.name: Early Action
rounds.policy: Nonbinding and open internationally. MIT imposes no additional-application restriction, but you must respect another college's restrictive or binding plan. Decisions: mid-December.

rounds.name: Regular Action
rounds.policy: Nonbinding; decisions in mid-March. One application per entry year; an EA denial cannot be followed by an RA application.

fee.waiver: International applicants may request a hardship waiver in the application's Fee Waiver Request section.

requirements.submission: MIT application portal

requirements.label: Four main written responses
requirements.submission: MIT application: interests, educational path, intended impact, unexpected challenge. About 100–200 words each; follow portal limits.

requirements.label: Four short written responses
requirements.submission: MIT application: enjoyment, admired person, favorite topic, breadth or depth of interests. About 40–50 words each.

requirements.label: Activities section

testing.text: SAT or ACT required; paper and digital SAT accepted. ACT writing/science and SAT essay are not required. Self-report all full sittings; MIT superscores and verifies on enrollment. No SAT/ACT minimum or recommended cutoff. C8 of the 2025–26 CDS specifically confirms required testing for Fall 2027.

scores.population: Enrolled first-time first-year students submitting each test; domestic and international combined.
scores.note: Historical middle 50%; SAT and ACT shares overlap. These are descriptive enrollee statistics, not admission thresholds.

english.text: Strongly recommended in the specified non-native-speaker circumstances, rather than required universally. Self-report full sittings; MIT verifies after enrollment. Published numeric minima and recommendations are distinct.

selection.text: MIT emphasizes academic preparation alongside collaboration, initiative, curiosity, thoughtful risk-taking, practical creativity and care for community. Depth and personal meaning matter more than collecting activities. The CDS categories describe general review, not a points formula.

funding.text: Need-blind admission and full demonstrated-need aid apply to domestic and international undergraduates. The institutional assessment may include a student work/savings contribution; a family-income policy is not an individual full-cost award.
funding.forms: CSS Profile and parental tax/income records through IDOC. FAFSA is for eligible domestic applicants, not applicants following MIT's international aid process.
funding.renewal: Apply each year with CSS Profile and income records by February 15; reassessment follows current family finances.
funding.exceptions: MIT's FAQ says international CSS fee waivers are unavailable. Ask Student Financial Services about individual obstacles. Late aid submissions are reviewed without a lateness penalty but must meet the academic-year final limit.

components.label: MIT health insurance if not waived (excluded)

costs.exclusions: Published total excludes individualized travel and separate health insurance. Housing/food are budget allowances; actual billed choices vary. The housing explanation retains an older room-price example; the 2026–27 table's $14,090 is used. Fall 2027 costs are not verified.

route.text: Choose one: Common Application or Apply Coalition with Scoir. QuestBridge is a separate eligibility-based route. Prior college coursework does not bar first-year application if all credits are forfeited and four full-time Amherst years are intended; holders of a bachelor's degree cannot apply.

rounds.name: Early Decision
rounds.policy: Binding first-choice plan; no other simultaneous ED application. If admitted, withdraw other applications. Decisions early to mid-December 2026.

rounds.name: Regular Decision
rounds.policy: Nonbinding. Decisions around March 20, 2027; enrollment response May 1, 2027.

fee.waiver: Request through Common App, Scoir or Amherst Quick Pass; confirm your eligibility in the chosen mechanism.

testing.text: SAT/ACT optional for the 2026–27 admission cycle. Self-reported scores are accepted; enrolled score-submitters must verify officially. Amherst superscores SAT and ACT. Enhanced ACT science is optional. Submit scores by your application deadline; current instructions take precedence over the older CDS receipt date.

scores.population: Enrolled first-time first-year students who submitted the respective test. The file's C1 describes Fall 2025, while C9 retains Fall 2024 wording.
scores.note: Published C9 figures, not a range for every enrollee or a cutoff. Test-optional submission selection affects interpretation; precise cohort label needs confirmation.

english.text: Required for relevant non-native speakers unless the most recent two secondary-school years were primarily taught in English. IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT/Home Edition and Duolingo accepted. The current international page allows self-reported superscores and requires official verification on enrollment. Listed scores are strongly recommended, not unconditional admission minima.

waiver.rule: Native English speakers, or first-year applicants whose two most recent secondary-school years used English as the primary instruction language. Claim eligibility through supplement questions or portal attestation; no other waiver grounds are listed.

selection.text: Amherst gives the greatest weight to the academic transcript: challenge, performance and sustained effort. Recommendations, writing, meaningful activities and optional submitted tests add context. No single component determines the decision.

funding.text: Need-blind admission and full calculated-need aid apply internationally. Initial offers exclude required student loans but can include student employment; this is not an automatic full-cost grant.
funding.forms: 2027–28 CSS or approved ISFAA, 2025 income records and conditional parent/business supplements. International documents go to Amherst's Financial Aid Portal rather than a universal IDOC workflow. FAFSA is not required for ineligible international students.
funding.renewal: Reapply annually; international returning-student materials are due March 1. Current income and family circumstances are reassessed. Outside awards can replace employment and some student contribution before reducing institutional scholarship.
funding.exceptions: North Korean applicants use ISFAA. Serious CSS fee hardship can qualify for ISFAA without reducing aid eligibility. Residence-specific instructions and the personalized portal control. A significant exchange-rate change can qualify for a review.

costs.exclusions: $98,160 is the sum of published direct costs and personal allowance, excluding variable travel, insurance and the one-time $25 transcript charge. Required course materials are already included. International travel allowance covers one round trip. Health insurance is added to an aided student's budget when applicable. Tuition insurance is separately billed and waivable.
